newsitem.title: FRANCE: French planters raise 96/97 sugar crop estimate.
newsitem.headline: French planters raise 96/97 sugar crop estimate.

text.p: French sugar beet planters said on Friday they revised upwards their estimate for the new 1996/97 sugar crop as rain and mild temperatures in October helped speed beet development.
Planters said they were now eyeing final sugar output of at least 4.05 million tonnes instead of a previous target of 4.01 million.
"Weather conditions were good in October. It rained but temperatures were mild. This helped both both beet weight and sugar content," an analyst for the French beet planters federation (CGB) said.
The new forecast was in line with the latest predictions from national sugar intervention board FIRS and the sugar manufacturers' association SNFS, he added.
But 1996/97 sugar output would still be below the 4.2 millon tonnes of sugar produced last year.
The latest FIRS estimate assumed a yield of 9.60 tonnes per hectare against 9.77 tonnes last year and area of 422,000 hectares against 430,000 hectares.
Data collected by the CGB up to November 3 showed some 75 percent of total beet area harvested and some 55 percent delivered to refineries.
Sugar content at delivery was 18.8 percent against 18.65 percent on October 20 and 17.5 percent on November 3, 1995.
Beet yield stood at 53.2 tonnes per hectare, up from 53 tonnes on October 20 but still down from 58 tonnes on November 3, 1995. --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5432
